Good to be with you. Thank you.
The Ukraine-Russia situation, what if anything could the United States have done differently to try to mitigate or try to avoid where we are right now?

Russia has been preparing for this for quite a while. We could have done sanctions last fall. I wrote the White House in November and I said, now is the time for lethal aid sales to Ukraine. It's the time for sanctions of their energy and economic sectors. time for a comprehensive, coordinated diplomatic message so that our allies know we're going to be there to support people that are our allies. And that is not what happened, but you know what, Tim, one would think. After what happened in Afghanistan, they would have gotten the diplomatic messaging right and would have been upfront with our allies. But here we find ourselves. Putin has felt emboldened because Biden didn't put any roadblocks up. Putin wanted a start treaty. He wanted a five-year renewal on that. Trump had told him he would give him one year, but it would be with conditions. Biden gives him five years, no conditions. He gives him Nord Stream, no conditions, so he feels like he's got a lot of runway.

turn_text: Which leads, I think, to a logical question when you mentioned Afghanistan and our disastrous exit there. We're renegotiating with Iran now, a Russia situation. How is America perceived around the rest of the globe

That is really interesting to think about because the handling of Afghanistan changed a lot of things. And Biden's perceived weakness has changed. what people have is kind of a U.S. foreign policy used to be clearly understood. And that is not the way it is right now. And I think Robert Gates had it right. Joe Biden's been wrong on every foreign policy issue for the last 40 years. In Afghanistan and Russia, he has clearly not made decisions that are serving the United States well. I am hopeful that our allies will stick with us, will stay coordinated. NATO meets Friday in a virtual summit. I am hopeful there's going to be a coordinated message that will come out of that. And I am very hopeful that President Biden is going to be strong. and resolute and move forward with sanctions and deal with Russia in the obviously the only way that Vladimir Putin knows to deal which is with a lot of strength and just saying no you're not going any further.

And looking at the moves that China is going to make, if Russia gets moved out of the SWIFT system, is China going to become their bank? Is China going to pick up and purchase all their fuel from Russia? Are they going to change that if we do sanctions there? Is China going to try to slow down the supply chain to the US? Are there going to be changes there? Are they going to try to adversely impact the supply chain for our allies? So the way Xi Jinping comes into this is going to tell us a lot as to the type frenemy deal that Russia and China have struck over trying to replace the US as a superpower.

You were a strong supporter of President Trump. You worked closely with him on several things. Would we be in a different position today? Would the world be in a different position today if President Trump were still president?

Indeed, they would. When you look at what Secretary Pompeo and President Trump were doing with Afghanistan, there was going to be a withdrawal, but it was conditions based, not time and calendar based. That is an enormous difference. It could have taken years. It could have gone very quickly, but it was all conditions based. very important. And there were certain metrics that would be achieved if Afghanistan made a move or we made a move. Then you look at dealing with Russia. Start, you have one year with conditions, or five years, no conditions. And the difference there, you wanted to hold Putin to account. sanctions on Nord Stream. And what is so interesting to me, Senator Cruz had the resolution as we were going to sanction Nord Stream and it was the White House that was pushing the Democrats to vote against that and not to contradict what they were trying to do. Well, you cannot negotiate, obviously, with Putin in the manner that they thought you could negotiate with him. You have to do things condition-space.
